title: Affine two-term determinant functors from good diagrams
statement: Fix coherent normalized derived pullback comparisons [lem-trf-two-term-determinant-pullback-coherence]. There exists an affine determinant system [def-trf-affine-determinant-interfaces]: finite projective two-term complexes give invertible determinant modules, every derived isomorphism acts by the kernel-normalized good-diagram map, and arbitrary affine scalar extension is natural and unital/associative. On pullbacks of displayed models from arbitrary schemes the exterior formula and zero trivialization form compatible families, and the identity complex has the evaluation normalization. This is only the affine algebra construction; it does not assert any determinant functor for non-affine schemes.

source.place: Tag 0FJM, using Tags 0FJI--0FJL; scalar extension and affine sheaf comparison in perfect.tex Tag 0FJY.

proof.text: On $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the Tor-window and affine-preimage lemmas give a pseudo-coherent preimage $C$. The tensor/tilde and homology comparisons reflect the given Tor interval $[-1,0]$ (the affine tilde unit is invertible). The projective-window lemma gives a good model $P$. Set $D(P)=\det P^0\otimes(\det P^{-1})^\vee$, invertible by the projective determinant lemma. K-projective Hom identifies derived isomorphisms and their inverses with homotopy classes of quasi-isomorphisms.

Choose a good diagram and set $D(a)=T_cT_b^{-1}$. Fibre-product composition gives $T_{c_{12}}T_r=T_{b_{23}}T_s$ by the surjective calculus, so the proposed maps multiply. A diagram for the identity has homotopic legs and map $1$. Compose any diagram for $a$ with one fixed diagram for its homotopy inverse: their composite is $1$, proving diagram independence. Homotopic $a$ share diagrams. Thus $D$ is functorial; transport along chosen model identifications $e_L:QP_L\cong L$ by $u\mapsto D(e_M^{-1}ue_L)$.

For $A\to B$: a surjective quasi-isomorphism $a$ of good complexes has split exact term sequences and kernel $N$ with $d_N$ invertible, so $B\otimes_A a$ is again one with kernel $B\otimes_AN$; homotopies tensor, so good diagrams go to good diagrams. The exterior/dual scalar comparisons commute with $\gamma^i$ and $\det(d_N)$, hence with $T_a$ and both legs of every good diagram. They give a natural $s:B\otimes D(P)\cong D(B\otimes P)$. Good models are K-flat; sheafify $s$ and follow it by the model comparison for $e_g=Lg^*(e_L)\varepsilon_g^{-1}$ to define pullbackIso. The fixed coherence identifies successive counits with the section tensor comparison. Thus its composition equation is the scalar associativity equation; its left unit law at the identity gives the scalar unit equation.

source.place: perfect.tex Tag 0FJY, scalar extension and normalized comparisons

proof.text: For a displayed $P$ on any $X$ and affine $f:Y\to X$, let $P_f=\Gamma(Y,f^*P)$: its terms are finite projective, and the affine tilde counit reconstructs $f^*P$. Put $j_f:Q(f^*P)\cong Lf^*QP$ equal to the inverse K-flat counit. Define local_modelIso by the sheafified wedge/dual scalar map followed by $D(j_f)$ and the chosen-model comparison. Local free frames define the wedge sheaf maps. For further $h$, their scalar associativity and the normalized equation for $\kappa_{h,f},j_f,j_h$ give local_model_naturality. Apply the same formula to the zero model for local_zeroIso and its naturality.

source.place: perfect.tex Tag 0FJY, displayed models and zero

proof.text: Choose the single global $z:Q[E\xrightarrow1E]\cong0$ induced by projection; its kernel and cokernel cohomology vanish. On every affine test scheme the counits identify its pullback with that projection. The surjective calculus contracts by $\delta=\det(1_E)$, giving evaluation (ordinary symmetry puts it in the required dual-first order). The scalar comparison preserves evaluation, so this proves local_acyclic for that same $z$, including rank zero. These are all fields of the affine interface.

Base item in live and side-live is unchanged and the 3 new ids are absent from both, so the delivery is not superseded. Item and new nodes are byte-identical to head e3c09861075f (FIX), apart from split_report, so that run's step-3 fix was lost. Step by step against the base: step 2 of the base (M, b, c, h(x,f)=p(f), c^0 surjective) and the fibre-product half of step 3 are now lem-trf-good-two-term-surjective-diagrams. I re-read 0FJM at more-algebra.tex l.37124 and checked the chain-map and homotopy identities, the fibre-product kernels with invertible differential, and the composite c23 s ≃ a'a b12 r. The module algebra of base step 5 is now lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons, checked for non-flat B, variable rank, V=0 and kernel-first γ. The new lem-trf-pseudo-coherent-tor-projective-window is the final clause of Stacks 0658 (l.18889, re-read); it supplies the global affine model that the base assumed. Step 1 reflects the [-1,0] Tor window through tensor-tilde (3), the homology comparison and the invertible unit τ. Independence (fixed diagram of the homotopy inverse), K-flatness, the j_f/κ local families and the single global z for local_acyclic stay in the item as assembly. No duplicates found (rg 0658/0FJM/good diagram/exterior scalar; ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect, bounded-finite-tor-perfect, site-perfect-tor-window, sifted-good-diagram-calculus, koszul-base-change-iso, flat-lci-presentation-base-change all differ). Closure of each flagged node: window 21 nodes, no trf/pod; diagrams 8 nodes, no trf/pod; scalar comparisons 197 nodes and the exact-sequence lemma 196, whose only trf nodes are def-trf-projective-determinant-module and the exact-sequence lemma itself. All are generic algebra (0658, 0FJM, 0FJB), not trace-formula or Poincaré steps, so accepted. The 12 declared tool_uses are generic affine/homological comparisons and are accepted.
